canonical_definition: In-Context Learning refers to the capability of large language models to adapt to tasks or improve performance by leveraging examples, instructions, or demonstrations provided in the input prompt during inference, without modifying model parameters. This often involves few-shot or one-shot learning, where the model learns patterns, rules, or output formats from the provided context to guide reasoning or generation. Some definitions emphasize dependencies on context length or mechanisms like induction heads for pattern recognition, while others highlight applications in resolving ambiguity, aligning outputs, or enabling task decomposition without manual intervention.
